A 35-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease secondary to IgA nephropathy underwent a living donor kidney transplantation at 33 years of age, with her mother serving as the donor. Her bilateral native kidneys had not been removed and remained in situ. The donor’s left kidney was implanted in the recipient’s right iliac fossa, with end-to-side anastomoses of the renal artery and vein to the external iliac artery and vein. An extravesical ureteroneocystostomy was performed according to the Lich-Gregoir technique with creation of a submucosal tunnel to provide an anti-reflux mechanism. The early postoperative course was uneventful, and graft function stabilized with a serum creatinine level of approximately 1.2 mg/dL (reference range for adult women in our laboratory: 0.46-0.79 mg/dL).
